rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The defenders of the treacherous are themselves people who deceive and betray their own souls.
rows.anchor: kendilerini aldatan, nefislerine hıyanet eden kimselersiniz

words: فَمَن يُجَٰدِلُ ٱللَّهَ عَنْهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one will plead for the traitors before God on Judgment Day or serve as their protecting advocate.
rows.anchor: olan yevm-i kıyâmette o hâinler tarafından kim mücadele edecek?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Defending the traitors does not save them; it makes their defenders share responsibility, betray themselves, and forfeit the Prophet’s intercession.
rows.anchor: onların mes’ûliyetlerine iştirak ederek nefsinize hıyanet etmiş ve kendinizi aldatmış oluyorsunuz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anyone who does wrong and then seeks God’s forgiveness will find Him forgiving and merciful.
rows.anchor: Allah’ı Gafûr, Rahîm bulur. Lâkin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s forgiveness should not be used as a pretext for presuming upon mercy or treating sin lightly.
rows.anchor: diye mağrurlanıp da günahı istihfaf etmemelidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sin damages the sinner’s own soul, and he alone bears its harm and burden.
rows.anchor: O günah ile bozulan kendi nefsidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every sin is a betrayal of one’s own soul, so one must guard against sin.
rows.anchor: Ve bunun için her günah nefse bir hıyanettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported distinction makes khatiʾa a minor sin and ithm a major sin.
rows.anchor: Birincisi hatîe sagīre, ism kebîredir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second distinction makes khatiʾa a sin whose harm stays with its doer and ithm a transgressive sin harming others.
rows.anchor: İkincisi hatîe yalnız yapanda kalan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third distinction treats khatiʾa as a wrong whether deliberate or accidental, while ithm is deliberate.
rows.anchor: ism ise ‘amden husûle gelendir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Falsely attributing one’s sin to an innocent person adds the grave sin of slander to the original offense; the wrongdoer should repent and seek reconciliation.
rows.anchor: Mâhiyet-i iftira birdir. Başkasına yapmadığı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tuʿma’s people knew he was the thief, yet came to defend him, secure his acquittal, and shift the theft onto a Jew.
rows.anchor: Tu‘me’nin kavmi onun sârık olduğunu bildikleri hâlde Peygamber’e gelmişler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their cooperation in sin, false testimony, and slander misguides only themselves and does the Prophet no harm.
rows.anchor: ve yalan yere şehâdet ve bühtan ile kendilerini dalâlete düşürüyorlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet would judge according to outward circumstances; a judge is not liable for a false result when contrary facts are neither known nor established.
rows.anchor: sen hükmünü zâhir-i hâle binâ edecektin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s favor here is the gift of prophethood, while His mercy is the Prophet’s preservation and protection from error.
rows.anchor: nübüvveti ve rahmeti, yani hıfz u ismeti olmasa idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revealed Book is a proof above every other proof, and wisdom is the foremost quality for correctness in knowledge and action.
rows.anchor: Kitab her delîlin fevkinde bir delil; hikmet, ilm ü amelde hakk u savâba isabet için en büyük bir haslet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divinely given inward knowledge reveals realities beyond appearances and preserves the Prophet from error and harm.
rows.anchor: bu ilm-i ledün zavâhirin mâverâsını gösteren ve zâhir u bâtında hatâdan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By this great favor, the Prophet judges with comprehensive prophethood and leadership, protected from error outwardly and inwardly.
rows.anchor: zâhir u bâtında hatâdan ma‘sum olarak hükmedersin

words: لَّا خَيْرَ فِى كَثِيرٍۢ مِّن نَّجْوَىٰهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most secret counsels of the traitors have no good; the exception is counsel urging charity, recognized good, or reconciliation among people.
rows.anchor: sadaka veya bir mâruf veya beyne’n-nâs bir ıslah emredenler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Charity provides material benefit, enjoining good provides spiritual benefit, and reconciliation prevents harm; together the three cover all beneficial deeds.
rows.anchor: Menfaat ise ya mal vermek gibi cismânîdir, sadaka ile bu nev‘e işaret olunmuştur

words: وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَٰلِكَ ٱبْتِغَآءَ مَرْضَاتِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised great reward attaches to doing the good deed itself and is conditioned on seeking God’s pleasure.
rows.anchor: Allah rızâsı için olmakla da takyid olunmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beneficial works that affect others either deliver benefit or avert harm.
rows.anchor: nâsa müte‘addî olan amel-i hayr ya îsâl-i menfaat veya def‘-i mazarrat içindir

words: وَمَن يُشَاقِقِ ٱلرَّسُولَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ مَا تَبَيَّنَ لَهُ ٱلْهُدَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After guidance has become clear through revelation, wisdom, and divinely disclosed realities, opposing the Messenger and following another path leads to Hell.
rows.anchor: Her kim bu suretle kendisine hak tebeyyün ettikten

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed when Tuʿma fled to Mecca and apostatized after God exposed his treachery and he refused to submit to the truth.
rows.anchor: Mekke’ye firar ve irtidad etmesi üzerine nâzil olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shiqāq and mushāqqa mean to separate off and enter into opposition.
rows.anchor: “şakk”dan, ayrılıp muhalefete geçmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers’ way is their path of monotheistic belief and sound religion in doctrine and practice, including obedience to God, His Messenger, and those in authority.
rows.anchor: itikad ve amelde mü’minlerin tuttuğu tarîk-ı tevhid ve dîn-i kayyimdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The additional clause explicitly makes adherence to the believers’ way a requirement alongside following the Messenger, even though opposition to him ordinarily entails leaving their way.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah’a ittibâ‘gibi sebîl-i mü’minîne ittibâ‘dahi sarâhaten matlubdur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Where a definitive text exists, opposing the Messenger and leaving the believers’ way coincide; where no text exists, the clause forecloses claims one may oppose consensus without opposing him.
rows.anchor: nas vârid olmayan husûsâtta bu telâzüm zâhir değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse makes following the community’s consensus obligatory and shows that guidance can become clear through consensus; Sunni scholars cite it as a proof for this duty.
rows.anchor: ulemâ-yı Ehl-i Sünnet ve Cemaat bu fıkrayı icmâ‘-ı ümmete ittibâ‘ın vücûbunu ifade için sevk olunmuş bir nas olarak anlamışlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording ittibāʿ shows that the issue turns on the principle of following or adherence.
rows.anchor: kelimesi de asıl meselenin tâbi‘iyet esası üzerinde deveran ettiğini gösterir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb iṣlāʾ means to cast something into fire and keep it there.
rows.anchor: “Islâ”, bir şeyi yakmak için ateşe atmak ve ateşe atıp durdurmaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apostate who opposes the Messenger after guidance and leaves the believers’ way faces Hell; this is not temporary or limited to Tuʿma-like apostates.
rows.anchor: Bunu muvakkat sanmamalı ve yalnız Tu‘me gibi mürtedlere mahsus da zannetmemelidir

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَغْفِرُ أَن يُشْرَكَ بِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel passage at 4:48 explains the People of the Book’s shirk through false claims that the Messiah or ʿUzayr is God’s son; here shirk is described as far misguidance.
rows.anchor: orada ٱلْمَسِيحُ ٱبْنُ ٱللَّهِ,عُزَيْرٌ ٱبْنُ ٱللَّهِ gibi ibn isnad ve iftirasına işaretle

words: وَمَن يُشْرِكْ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدْ ضَلَّ ضَلَٰلًۢا بَعِيدًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shirk is both a grave falsehood against God and an extreme departure from truth, far from divine forgiveness and mercy; in either case it is great injustice and is unforgiven without repentance.
rows.anchor: şirk hem hakka bir iftira ve ism-i azîm hem de bir dalâl-i ba‘îddir. Ve her iki surette zulm-i azîmdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book’s shirk is more marked by slander and moral corruption, while other polytheists’ shirk is more marked by misguidance and ignorance.
rows.anchor: Ehl-i kitâbın şirki dalâletten ziyade bir eser-i iftirâ, diğerlerinin şirki iftirâdan ziyade bir eser-i dalâlettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whose shirk stems from ignorance may abandon it through intellectual progress, whereas those driven by immorality can deepen their rebellion as their knowledge grows.
rows.anchor: cehaletten münba‘is olan şirk erbâbının terakkiyât-ı ilmiye ve akliye ile şirkten vazgeçmeleri melhuz olduğu hâlde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The People of the Book disputed after knowledge came to them, illustrating how knowledge can accompany increased rebellion when moral will is corrupt.
rows.anchor: Bundan dolayıdır ki ehl-i kitab hakkında

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge alone does not ensure faith or good conduct: will, passions, anger, envy, habit, hope, despair, and pride can turn a person against truths he knows.
rows.anchor: iman için sade marifet kâfi olmadığı gibi, te’mînât-ı ahlâkiye için de sade ilim kâfi değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Devil exemplifies intelligent rebellion, and ordinary people’s shirk can result from being deceived by schemers who distort truth.
rows.anchor: İblis bunun en büyük misâli, şeytanet de bu mânanın menba‘ve masdarıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The love of women is described as the strongest arouser of desire and a powerful means of deception.
rows.anchor: زُيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ حُبُّ ٱلشَّهَوَٰتِ مِنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After explaining the two kinds of shirk through false attribution and misguidance, the commentary develops the far-misguidance theme in a way suited to Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.
rows.anchor: Sûre-i Nisâ mevzû‘u ile mütenâsib olmak üzere şu suretle îzah olunuyor

rows.speaker: Ekser müfessirîn
rows.claim: Most commentators identify Adam’s two sons as his biological sons Qābil and Hābil.
rows.anchor: Ekser müfessirîn bu iki Âdem oğlu Hazret-i Âdem’in sulbî oğulları olan Kābil ve Hâbil olduğunu söylemişler

rows.speaker: Hasan ve Dahhâk
rows.claim: Hasan and Dahhāk identify them as two Israelites, using the story’s later phrase “because of that” as evidence.
rows.anchor: Hasan ve Dahhâk ise kıssanın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exact identities are unnecessary to benefit from the account: the general wording emphasizes the event rather than legends, and even a hypothetical story would have a true application in Israelite history.
rows.anchor: kıssadan istifade için eşhâsın ta‘yîn-i hüviyetleri lâzım olmadığından ale’l-ıtlâk

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because many marvel-filled tales circulate under Qābil and Hābil’s names, “in truth” directs attention to the event’s reality rather than fables.
rows.anchor: بِٱلْحَقِّ kaydıyla da efsanelere değil, zât-ı vak‘anın hakikatine celb-i dikkat edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says God gave people the two sons of Adam as a parable and told them to take its good and leave its evil.
rows.anchor: Bir hadîs-i şerifte vârid olmuştur ki: “Allah teâlâ size iki Âdemoğlu ile bir mesel darb etti, bunun hayrını tutun, şerrini bırakın.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurbān is not limited to a slaughtered animal; it means anything offered to draw near to God, including sacrifices and other alms.
rows.anchor: asıl mânası Allah’a tekarrub için arz u takdim edilen herhangi bir şey demektir ki gerek zebîha ve gerek diğer sadakalardan e‘amdır

words: فَتُقُبِّلَ مِنْ أَحَدِهِمَا وَلَمْ يُتَقَبَّلْ مِنَ ٱلْءَاخَرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One offering was accepted and the other was not; the rejected brother envied the accepted one and threatened to kill him.
rows.anchor: kurbanı kabul edilmeyen öbürüne hased ederek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The brother answers that God accepts only from the God-fearing, urging his attacker to fear God and correct his intention.
rows.anchor: Allah ancak müttakīlerden kabul eder. Binâen‘aleyh Allah’tan kork, niyetini tashih et

words: مَآ أَنَا۠ بِبَاسِطٍۢ يَدِىَ إِلَيْكَ لِأَقْتُلَكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He refuses to raise his hand to kill his brother because he fears God, Lord of all worlds.
rows.anchor: Çünkü ben, Rabbü’l-âlemîn olan Allah’tan her hâlde korkarım

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second difficulty is how a pious person can wish for either his own disobedience or another person’s sin.
rows.anchor: istemek câiz olmadığı gibi, başkasının isyanını istemek de câiz değildir

words: إِنِّىٓ أُرِيدُ أَن تَبُوٓأَ بِإِثْمِى وَإِثْمِكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred sense is not that he wishes his brother to sin, but that he warns him not to make either of them sin and tells him to desist.
rows.anchor: Bu sözden asıl maksad öbürünün günaha girmesini istemek değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His warning concludes that the killer will return bearing the sins and be among the people of the Fire, the recompense of wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: bu iki günahı yüklenerek can verip

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first difficulty is how a killer can bear his victim’s sin when no bearer carries another’s burden.
rows.anchor: Bu nokta birkaç vechile îzah edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says in a mutual exchange of insults the initiator bears his own words and an equivalent burden for causing the other’s, unless the victim exceeds the limit.
rows.anchor: sövüşenlerin bütün söyledikleri bâdi’e aittir. Yani ibtidâ başlayan hem aynen kendisinin günahını, hem de sebep olduğundan dolayı arkadaşının günahının bir mislini yüklenir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this explanation, “my sin” is the equivalent sin the speaker would incur by retaliating; the initiator then bears two crimes, while a non-retaliating victim avoids the retaliatory one.
rows.anchor: biri tecavüz eder diğeri de mukābele eyler de ikisi de maktul düşecek olursa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reads “my sin” elliptically as the sin of killing me and “your sin” as the killer’s prior sin, such as the offense behind his rejected offering.
rows.anchor: بِإِثْمِى demek hazf-i muzâf ile إثمُْ قـَتْلِي yani “beni öldürmek günahı”, وَإِثْمِكَ de “bundan evvelki günahın

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas, İbn Mes‘ud, Hasan ve Katâde
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Masʿūd, Hasan, and Qatāda are reported for the alternative reading of the two sins as murder and the killer’s earlier offense.
rows.anchor: bu mâna İbn Abbas, İbn Mes‘ud, Hasan ve Katâde hazerâtından nakil de edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second answer says that although one may not wish for another’s sin, one may wish that a sinner receive punishment if he persists.
rows.anchor: âsînin ikāb ve tecziyesini istemek câizdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the first answer: the speaker’s aim is admonition and preventing sin, not wishing sin upon his brother.
rows.anchor: demek de olabilir. Fakat evvelki daha muvâfıktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoer’s soul made fratricide seem easy, unobstructed, and appealing, even as if it were an obedient act; it eased and encouraged the crime.
rows.anchor: böyle büyük bir cinayeti güya bir tâat sevkiyle endişesiz yapılabilecek, mâni‘den âzâde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taṭwīʿ here is the causative form of ṭawʿ, expressing that the soul rendered the murder compliant and easy for him.
rows.anchor: Burada tatvî‘bu mânaca “tav‘”dan tef‘îldir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom “the pasture was spread for him” means there was plenty before him to graze as he wished; here murder was presented like a ready pasture.
rows.anchor: طاَعَ لَهُ الْمَرْتَعُ derler ki “istediği gibi otlamak için otlak önüne bol bol seriliverdi” demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He killed his brother and became one of the losers, gaining no benefit and suffering loss in both religion and worldly life.
rows.anchor: kendisine bir fâide temin etmek ihtimâli olmadıktan başka dininde de dünyasında da ziyan etti
